title: [Tool] Seamline Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Seamline Topstitch. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** → All sewing lines on the Pattern are displayed. 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The Topstitch is now being created with being highlighted. **※ Note:** * Click and drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. title: Auto Sewing (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Patterns are automatically sewn based on their placement on avatars. **※Note:** The available range of automatic sewing is as follows, * Garment: * Top (T-shirts, jackets, Jumper, etc.) and One-piece are possible. * Bottom (Skirt, Pants, etc) and Pants are impossible. * Parts: Bodies, Sleeves, Collars, Darts, Pleats, Cuffs, Sleeves with Vend & Placket. * Layers: One-ply patterns such as Pockets and Lining except for two-layer Patterns. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ojB6NZU7q14 **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Auto Sewing** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Auto Sewing** **Operation** 1. Click the [Arrangement Points ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001999287-Arrange-Pattern-with-Arrangement-Points-Flip-Wrap-Direction)of the Avatar to arrange the Pattern. Since Auto Sewing is calculated by the information of the Arrangement Points (where each Pattern Piece is arranged), correct Arrangement Points should be used based on the rules below, Otherwise, Auto Sewing may not work properly. (It is only applicable to the Bounding Volumes provided by CLO) **Collar/ Band** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's neck. ---|--- **Bodies** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's body. **Sleeves** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's arm, the cuffs can be used either arm/wrist Arrangement Points. **Bottom (ver 6.1)** | Use Arrangement Points at the legs. **※Note:** Be mindful to arrange the pieces to auto sew correctly. \- If the belt length includes a placket which is placed over the zipper, arrange the placket piece. \- Trace the internal line of the side pocket along side seams. \- If the pants width is large, arrange front and back pattern pieces separately by using each of the arrangement points. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The arranged patterns are automatically sewn. **※Note:** * If sewing has been applied prior to automatic sewing, it is maintained while the rest of the sewing lines are being additionally auto-sewn. * Darts and Pleats can be sewn automatically without arranging patterns. * For Pleats, automatic sewing is possible only when Internal Lines are defined by the fold direction of the Pleats.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on automatically sewing patterns for garments using avatar arrangement points, detailing the types of garments supported and the correct procedures for optimal results.

title: Layer Clone (Over)
content: **Layer Clone (Over)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aX8rz_DrydA \- Duplicate a Pattern in its draped state and place it directly over the original Pattern. Sewing Lines will be automatically applied to the Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to connect the cloned Pattern to the original Pattern. \- The Layer Clone (Under) function is efficient when creating a double-layered Garment such as padding, collar, cuffs, and more. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern to be cloned and select **Layer Clone (Over)** from the pop-up menu. \- The cloned Pattern will follow along the mouse. Click on the 2D window to place the cloned Pattern. \- In the 3D window, the cloned Pattern will be directly placed over the original Pattern and its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines will be sewn to the original Pattern. \- The cloned Patterns will be highlighted in light green in the 2D window and the linked editing will be applied.
content_description: Discover how to efficiently duplicate and layer patterns in CLO 3D using the Layer Clone (Over) function for seamless garment creation.

title: Strengthen/Unstrengthen
content: **Objective** The Pattern Strengthen is a feature that temporarily applies hard properties to the garment. When a pattern is folded, it can be folded more reliably by receiving a strong force from the line segment applied with the folding angle and if a garment is simulated by overlapping each other, it can be solved by simulating flat with the rigid force of the physical properties. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click the **Strengthen/Unstrengthen**. → The pattern will be strengthened/unstrengthened. **※Note:** Right-click on the background of the 3D window and hover **Show/Hide Color** **▶** Click the Show **Strengthen** Menu to show or hide the color applied during strengthening. (ver 6.1)
content_description: The Pattern Strengthen feature enhances garment simulation by temporarily applying rigid properties for improved reliability in folding and overlapping patterns.

title: Synchronize Pattern
content: **Objective** **ver2.3.0** All adjustments made in the 2D window **automatically** synchronizes with the 3D window. Simulation automatically ends when making a modification on 2D Pattern while simulating. **ver2.2.0** Once the sync button is activating, any adjustments, not only design adjustments, but also sewing lines, print textures, particle distances get reflected in the 3D window. Even if the synchronization is off, activating the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005481127/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulation** tool auto-activates the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** tool and reflects on the 3D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) ### **Operation** 1\. Make adjustments in the 2D window. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) **※ Note:****** **Changes in a Pattern Color According to Synchronization** A Pattern that has never been synchronized appears in transparent. A Pattern that has been synchronized at least once appears in red color, and a Pattern that its synchronization is currently activating appears in blue color.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for synchronizing adjustments between the 2D and 3D windows in the CLO 3D software, ensuring seamless updates during design modifications.

title: Can I use Patterns constructed in CLO in the manufacturing process?
content: **Question** Can I use Patterns constructed in CLO in the manufacturing process? **Answer** With slight modification, Patterns created in CLO can be used in the manufacturing process.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on the applicability of CLO-created patterns in the manufacturing process, highlighting necessary modifications for effective use.

title: Edit Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Edit Patterns Replace Patterns ## Objective Open and edit Patterns in provided Blocks from the Modular Configurator or replace them with your own. Location Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** ## **Operation** **Edit Patterns** 1. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 3. Select a Block to edit in the list of the Block Editor. → Remaining Blocks are frozen. 4. Modify it with the**![edit_pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026694688/edit_pattern.png) Edit Pattern **tool. 5. Once the modification is done, Simulate the according Block when the rest of the Blocks are still frozen. 6. Once the modification is completed, reselect the selected Block. → All of the Blocks are activated again. **Replace Patterns** 1. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶**Block Editor** 3. Locate Patterns out of Block Boxes or delete them. → The Block Boxes remain in light grey. 4. Add desired Garment files to substitute with. 5. Click and drag the Patterns that are just loaded to matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked with the Block Boxes. 6. Sew the Patterns to Block Boxes. 7. Select the according Block in the Block Editor, freeze the rest, then **Simulate**. **※ Note: ** * Selected Blocks in the Block Editor are also selected in the 2D window. * Editing Pattern in the Modular Mode is the same as the Simulation Mode. Deleting a segment or a point in a Pattern also deletes Sewing Lines between the Pattern and the Block Box. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to edit or replace patterns within Blocks using the Modular Configurator's Block Editor.

title: Apply Grading
content: **List of Contents** Apply Grading Apply Existing Size Group Create and Apply Size Group **Apply Grading YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMLzEdvNVWY** \- Create multiple sizes for Patterns by adding Size Group. \- Apply Existing Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ ![____17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182548/____17.png)**Assign to Selected Pattern** button next to the Size Group Create and Apply Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ **Assign To New Rule** **Apply Existing Size GroupYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r6t7cLM3sGg** \- With the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182068/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png)**Transform Pattern** tool, select Pattern to apply existing Size Group. \- Then, click ![____17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182548/____17.png)**Assign to Selected** **Pattern** button next to the desired Size Group from the Object Browser. \- Assigned grading appears in pink highlight when the Size Group is selected. **Create and Apply Size GroupYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o2SW-gMWAtI** \- With the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182068/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png)**Transform Pattern** tool, select Pattern to apply a new Size Group. \- Click **Assign To New Rule** button on the right top of the Object Browser to create and apply a new Size Group to the selected Pattern. ※Note : Grading information will be maintained even after the Patterns are Cut(ver.4.2.0). content_description: This web page provides guidance on applying grading and size groups to patterns in CLO 3D, including instructional videos and step-by-step instructions for creating and assigning size groups.

title: Particle Distance Setting
content: ### **Objective** Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance** **Operation** 1. Select Pattern(s). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance ** 3. Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') 4. Press Enter on keyboard to apply.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on adjusting Particle Distance in garment patterns to optimize simulation speed and quality during the design process.

title: Trace
content: **List of Contents** Trace Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as an Internal Shape Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as a Pattern Trace with Guidelines **Trace** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x9H8bsVBdVw \- Trace Baselines, Internal Lines and Pattern outlines as Internal Lines and Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022745867/mceclip0.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace.** ** Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-V27Rbjo5Yw **\- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rlYl0l0fn2k ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** or**Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=58R-Uhtuka4 ** \- To trace Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines as a shape, all selected lines need to be joined. \- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select multiple items. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3BoMdZaXDXQ ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose Trace as **Internal Lines/ Shapes** or **Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Trace as an Internal Shape YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=giYuoBwZzgk ** \- Use this option extract a closed shape as the shape created by the intersecting lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form the desired shape. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Shape**. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png)**Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the shape just traced. \- The closed shape will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TANzamZaeXY ** \- Use this option to trace intersecting lines as individual and separated lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines to be traced. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Lines/ Shapes.** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the lines just traced. \- Each traced lines will be selected individually. **Trace as a Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y8252WGNMRQ \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form a shape. \- Right-click on the selected items and choose **Trace as Pattern.** \- To trace a shape as a Pattern, all lines’ ends need to be adjoining each other. \- When more than three intersecting lines are selected, a shape formed by them will be traced as a Pattern. **Trace with Guidelines_ver.5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNLxAuFTYUM \- Select guidelines with Internal Lines or Pattern Outlines, and then right click to select the desired Trace option. \- Make sure to right click on the Internal Line or the Pattern Outline when tracing with guidelines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to utilizing the Trace tool in 2D pattern design, detailing various tracing methods supported by instructional videos.

title: Internal Rectangle Tool
content: ### **Objective** Create a rectangle inside a Pattern. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle** ** Operation** **Create Internal Rectangle** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle ** 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an Internal Rectangle. **※ Note:** * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a square (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a square Internal Shape by its center point (ver.5.1.0). 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Rectangle. **Create Internal Rectangle with Measurement Input** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle ** 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Rectangle window appears. 3. Enter appropriate values in the options indicated below. **Width** | Set width of an Internal Rectangle. ---|--- **Height** | Set height of an Internal Rectangle. **![__.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005595747/__.png) **| Link width and height to adjust them in a fixed ratio. **Position** | **Outline** | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the outline of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). **Center** | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the center of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0).
content_description: Learn how to create and customize an internal rectangle within a pattern using the Clo3D software's 2D toolbar and measurement input options.

title: Distribute
content: **Objective** Distribute Patterns or/and Internal Shapes/Lines by designated intervals (ver2.5.0). ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶**Horizontally** /**Vertically** ** Operation** 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001010987/1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001011007/2.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Lines/Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ **Horizontally** /**Vertically** →The Distribute Window appears. 4. Enter the desired Spacing value and select **OK**. →The selected Patterns and/or Internal Lines/Shapes are distributed horizontally or vertically by the designated intervals.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for efficiently distributing patterns and internal shapes or lines at specified intervals using the right-click pop-up menu in the 2D toolbar.

title: 2D Snapshot
content: **List of Contents** 2D Snapshot Apply 2D Snapshot Save 2D Snapshot **2D Snapshot** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WxAcbVh0-tk \- Save Patterns in 1:1 ratio as images. \- Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Patterns(1:1).** **Apply 2D Snapshot** \- The 2D window expands and the 2D Snapshot window appears. * **Size**** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y-26CJkEgbA ** * Preset Select one among provided Presets. * Orientation Decide orientation of the image. * Width, Height Type in desired Width and Height for the image. * Resolution Assign Resolution for the image. * **Option**** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YOpEVFuKVk0 ** * Select which lines will be included in the exported image. * Select which images will be included in the exported image. * Select additional information included in the exported image. * Save the image with transparent background. **Save 2D Snapshot** * **Save as .****Png YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E-XzQW9s4zY ** * Configure all options, click Save, and select the Save as Type as .png. * **Save as .****Pdf YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pbdZO__htwA ** * Configure all options, click Save, and select the Save as Type as .pdf. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply and save 2D snapshots of patterns, including options for image configuration and formats.

title: Freeze
content: **List of Contents** Freeze Result of Freeze Features of Freeze **Freeze** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4b6PvvL1Aiw \- Freeze selected Patterns to fix them like a hardware. \- Select desired Patterns to be frozen and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Freeze.** ** Result of Freeze** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U_A2cde9zL8 \- When the selected Patterns are frozen, the Patterns will turn light-blue. When the Simulation is activated, Patterns be fixed in the 3D environment. \- To unfreeze the selected Patterns, right click again and select **Unfreeze.** **Features of Freeze** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dsQeCexbeLY \- Frozen Patterns will be calculated for collision because they are considered as hard objects like Avatars. \- Therefore, activated Patterns cannot freely pass through the frozen Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides an overview of the Freeze feature, including how to freeze and unfreeze patterns, the visual results of freezing, and the implications for collision detection within a 3D environment.

title: Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing)
content: **List of Contents** Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) Result of Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) Features of Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) **Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A9uHEzBSUxo \- Deactivate selected Patterns and their Sewing lines to easily perform meticulous editing on the 3D Garment. \- Select desired Patterns to be deactivated and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing). ** Result of Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vpthmvkl9J8 \- When the selected Patterns and Sewing Lines are properly deactivated, Patterns should turn translucent navy while the Sewing Lines turn white. Even when the Simulation is activated, deactivated Patterns and Sewing Lines will not move and activated Patterns will not be sewn to the deactivated Patterns. \- To activate the selected Patterns and Sewing Lines, right click again and select **Activate.** **Features of Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lOZxI_e6bDw \- Deactivated Patterns will not be calculated for collision. \- Simulate overlapped Patterns, one being activated and the other being deactivated. The activated Pattern will easily pass through the deactivated Pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to deactivate patterns and sewing lines in 3D garment design, including step-by-step instructions, visual results, and key features to enhance your editing experience.

title: 2D Pattern (PACX) Open/Add/Save
content: **Objective** Save 2D Patterns as *.pacx file format. This format can only be saved or reopened and edited in CLO. ** Location** **Open Pattern** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Pattern ****Add Pattern ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ **Pattern ****Save Pattern ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Pattern** ** Operation** **Open Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Pattern** → The Open File window is opened. 2. Select the desired file and click the **Open** button. **Add Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶**Pattern** → The Add Pattern window is opened 2. Select the file to add and click the **Open** button to add the Pattern file. **Save Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Pattern** → The Save File window is opened. 2. Select a location to save the Pattern file to, type in a name and press the **Save** button. → A *.pacx file is created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for saving, opening, and adding 2D patterns in the *.pacx file format exclusively compatible with CLO software.

title: Replace as Pattern Outline
content: ### **Objective** Substitute Pattern outlines with Internal Lines, establishing the Internal Line as the new Pattern outline. ### **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008329508/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** ### **Operation** 1. [Create an internal line](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000481707) to be substituted with the Pattern outline. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008329508/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** 3. Click on the Internal Line and the Pattern outline that should be replaced. → The Internal Line and Pattern outline are highlighted in yellow. 4. Right-click on the selected Internal Line or Pattern outline. → A pop-up menu appears. 5. Select the**Replace as Pattern Outline** option. → The selected Pattern outline is replaced with the shape of the Internal Line. → The original Pattern outline appears as a Reference Line.
content_description: This web page serves as a step-by-step guide for substituting Pattern outlines with Internal Lines in the 2D Toolbar, transforming the Internal Line into the new Pattern outline.

title: Import - DXF
content: **List of Contents** Import DXF Import (Add) DXF **Import DXF** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8BE80_y7Z0 \- CLO is compatible with most of Pattern CAD such as YUKA, Gerber, Lectra, StyleCAD, Optitex, and PAD System in DXF-AAMA and DXF-ASTM file formats. \- Import 2D Patterns to use in CLO. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import ▶ **DXF (AAMA/ASTM). ** \- Locate the DXF file and select **Open.** \- The Import DXF window will appear. \- **Load Type** : Select either to open or add the DXF file. \- **Scale** : select the unit used to create the Patterns. When the **Auto Scale** option is selected, CLO will detect the unit of the Patterns automatically. \- **Rotation** : select the direction that the Patterns will be rotated to. -**Option** : Check following options as needed: Import Pattern Annotation, Auto-Trace as Internal Lines, Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line, Auto Distribute, and Optimize All Curve Points. \- Select OK to open the Patterns based on the settings. ** Import (Add) DXF** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mDZ7wFc5Af4 \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ **DXF (AAMA/ASTM). ** \- Locate the DXF file and select **Open.** \- The selected DXF file will be added to the workspace. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing DXF files into CLO, including step-by-step instructions and helpful YouTube video tutorials.
